headline: Leadership is taking responsibility for outcomes and enabling others to succeed—not just being in charge
universal_truth: Authority is granted; leadership is earned through service, vision, and results
fun_facts: Studies show that the most effective leaders spend more time listening than talking
Leadership without authority is often more influential than authority without leadership
The word 'lead' originally meant 'to go first'—leaders were those who went ahead into danger
discussion_questions: What's the difference between being a boss and being a leader?
Who has led you effectively, and what made them effective?
Where in your life are you already a leader?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Leadership isn't a title—it's a function. You can lead without authority and have authority without leading. Leaders take responsibility for outcomes, create direction, and enable others to succeed. It's service, not status.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We often confuse leadership with being in charge. But many people in charge don't lead, and many leaders have no formal authority. What does leadership actually involve?

options.text: Leaders create vision, take responsibility for outcomes, remove obstacles for others, and make decisions that benefit the group
options.response: Yes. Leadership is about the group's success, not personal glory. Leaders point direction, take blame when things fail, share credit when things succeed, and enable others to do their best work.

options.text: Leaders make decisions and tell people what to do
options.response: Decision-making is part of it, but leadership is more about enabling than commanding...

q1.title: Service Orientation
q1.script: Great leaders serve their teams, not the reverse. They ask 'what do you need to succeed?' and remove obstacles. The leader's job is making others effective. This inverted view of leadership is counterintuitive but powerful.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Service Orientation"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Vision and Direction
q2.script: Leaders provide clarity. Where are we going? Why does it matter? Without vision, effort scatters. Leaders don't have to invent the vision alone—but they must articulate it clearly enough that others can follow.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Asymmetric Credit
q3.script: Effective leaders give credit and take blame asymmetrically. When things go well: 'The team did it.' When things fail: 'I'm responsible.' This builds trust and psychological safety. People will follow someone who has their back.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Authority is granted; leadership is earned. True leadership comes through service, vision, and results—not titles. You can start leading anywhere you are.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 200—200 days of learning! 🎉 Tomorrow, we'll explore trusting others. Until then, consider: where can you lead by serving, regardless of your title?
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Service Leadership - Enable Someone
growTrack.activity: Today, help someone else succeed. Ask what obstacles they face and remove one. Give credit for their work. Leadership isn't about position—it's about making others more effective. You can lead from anywhere.
